title: Sub-128-Bit Key Recovery for ELmD(10,10)
summary: The paper refutes ELmD's claimed 128-bit security for the AES6 version, while a sub-128-bit key-recovery attack on ELmD(10,10) remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Can $\operatorname{ELmD}(10,10)$ be attacked for key recovery with time complexity below $2^{128}$?

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of the ELmD authenticated-encryption construction instantiated with 10-round AES.
parameters: ELmD(10,10): target instantiation based on 10-round AES
2^128: time-complexity threshold that a key-recovery attack must beat
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether ELmD(10,10) admits a key-recovery attack with time complexity below 2^128.

citations.label: Universal Forgery and Key Recovery Attacks on ELmD Authenticated Encryption Algorithm

progress.summary: The paper refutes the claimed 128-bit plaintext and key-recovery security for the AES6 version and applies its attacks only to that instantiation. It provides no sub-128-bit key-recovery attack for AES10-based ELmD(10,10).
citation_labels: Asli Bay et al., Universal Forgery and Key Recovery Attacks on ELmD Authenticated Encryption Algorithm
